title: Opportunistic infections
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's infection (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for painful swallowing.

HPI
Pt is an 80 y.o. female presenting for f/u of esophagitis. Pt reports persistent odynophagia, specifically when consuming solid foods. Symptoms have been ongoing since recent endoscopic evaluation. Pt currently taking fluconazole as prescribed. She notes some improvement in pain but reports it is still present. No fever, chills, or unintended weight loss reported. Denies any new respiratory symptoms or abdominal pain.

Medication List
Fluconazole 200mg daily
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Amlodipine 5mg daily

Review of Systems
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or fatigue.
HEENT: No sore throat or mouth sores.
Respiratory: No cough or shortness of breath.
GI: Positive for odynophagia. No nausea or vomiting.
MSK: No joint pain or swelling.
Neuro: No dizziness or confusion.

Social History
Retired. Lives with daughter. Independent with ADLs. No tobacco use. Occasional alcohol.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, stroke.
Father: Heart disease.

Vitals
BP: 132/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Ht: 12.4
WBC: 8.2
HbA1c: 5.8%

Exam
General: Alert and oriented x3. Well-appearing.
HEENT: Mucous membranes moist. No oral lesions noted.
Neck: Supple, no lymphadenopathy.
Respiratory: CTAB.
Cardiovascular: RRR, no murmurs.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended.
Throat: Mild erythema noted.

Assessment
1. Candida esophagitis. Pt is currently on fluconazole. Progressing slowly but still symptomatic.

Plan
1. Continue fluconazole as prescribed.
2. Maintain current diet as tolerated.
3. Follow up in 2 weeks to reassess symptoms and progress of candidal infection.

Electronically signed,
T. Haddad, NP
05/14/2026

distractors.why: Esophagitis, not only the mouth, is documented (HCC 6).
